question_bank.stem: Why, according to the lecture, did deep learning pull ahead as more data and compute became available?

options.text: Because larger neural networks kept improving with scale while older methods flattened out.
Because neural networks stopped needing large datasets once GPUs became common.
Because transformers made model size irrelevant as long as the optimizer was modern.
Because classical methods improve fastest exactly when datasets become enormous.

question_bank.rationale: Ng contrasts traditional methods that plateau with larger neural networks that continue improving as data and compute scale.

frame_evidence.visual_description: Whiteboard plot of performance vs. data, with older methods flattening while the larger-neural-network curve keeps rising.

question_bank.stem: In the course map drawn on the board, which layering matches how the lecture positioned deep learning?

options.text: Computer science fundamentals on top of deep learning, with machine learning under both.
Generative AI under machine learning, with deep learning as a separate side branch.
Computer science fundamentals -> machine learning -> deep learning -> generative AI.
Deep learning -> computer science fundamentals -> generative AI -> machine learning.

question_bank.rationale: The lecture explicitly stacks CS fundamentals under machine learning, machine learning under deep learning, and generative AI on top.

source_ref.evidence_span: So CS fundamentals, machine learning, deep learning,
